prompt: A survey of $200$ students records grade level (9th, 10th, 11th, 12th) and favorite lunch option. In the two-way table, the row for 10th graders has a total of $50$ students and the column for "pizza" has a total of $80$ students. For a chi-square test of independence, what is the expected count in the (10th grade, pizza) cell?
explanation: If grade level and lunch choice are independent, 10th graders should like pizza at the same rate as everyone: $80/200 = 40\%$.
The formula $\frac{50 \times 80}{200} = 20$ says the same thing.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two routes, one answer
steps: Column view: tenth graders are $50/200 = 25\%$ of the school, so expect $25\%$ of the 80 pizza fans: $20$.
Row view: pizza is chosen by $40\%$ of students, so expect $40\%$ of 50 tenth graders: $20$.
